description: None of the 4 spawn-register.test.js cases feed a malformed additive field (e.g. `tags:[123]`, `revenue_today_usd > revenue_mo_usd`, negative `revenue_by_source` value) through `registerSpawn` end-to-end. The spec's own verification-architecture table only cross-references sprint-1's generic schema tests, but S9 is a NEW call site that gates the store with these exact fields per S7.2/R9; nothing proves `registerSpawn` itself rejects (and never calls the store for) a malformed additive-field payload -- only that a signer mismatch is caught. If `verifyTelemetry`'s internal `validate()` call were ever bypassed by a future refactor of spawn-register.js, this gap would not be caught by the sprint-2 suite.

evidence.snippet: // 4 tests: byte-identical message, id-lowercase upsert, signer-mismatch throw, last_heartbeat stamp -- none exercise a schema-invalid additive field

fix: Add: `test("S9.1: throws and does NOT call the store when tags contains a non-string", ...)` with `basePayload({ tags: ["ok", 5] })`, asserting `stub.calls.length === 0`.
